methodological_rigor.justification: This is an exploratory biomarker sub-study embedded in the randomized NADIM II phase 2 trial (NCT03838159, 2:1 randomization) with 60 of 73 resected patients (82%) evaluable and 83/86 samples (97.5%) passing QC across three batches. Pre-specified methods include Cox proportional hazards with Schoenfeld-residual testing, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, Chi-square/Fisher, and — importantly — likelihood-ratio testing to formally evaluate incremental prognostic value of MRD over pCR. Censoring at non-cancer deaths is clearly described. Limitations acknowledged: modest sample, post-hoc analysis, not originally powered for MRD, and single-platform (Guardant Reveal) tumor-agnostic assay.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study is an exploratory analysis within an individual randomized controlled trial (NADIM II), which places the parent study at Oxford LoE 1b; the MRD sub-analysis inherits 1b because it is a pre-specified exploratory biomarker objective in a prospectively randomized cohort (although MRD-specific hypotheses were not pre-designed). Clinical relevance is high: MRD negativity at two serial time points identifies non-pCR patients with outcomes comparable to pCR patients, which is directly actionable for adjuvant de-escalation trial design.

reporting_quality.justification: As a prognostic biomarker study, REMARK is the applicable standard. Most REMARK items are addressed: study design, patient population, clinical characteristics (Table 1), assay details (Guardant Reveal, >20,000 DMRs, LOQ 0.01%), pre-specified statistical methods, and handling of competing events (non-cancer deaths censored). HRs with 95% CIs and P values are reported for all key comparisons. Data availability is moderate: MRD results per sample are provided as Supplementary Data S1, but there is no raw sequencing data repository cited and the proprietary Guardant Reveal pipeline is not open.

novelty_literature.justification: The study demonstrates that a tumor-agnostic epigenomic MRD assay (Guardant Reveal) refines prognostic stratification beyond pCR specifically in the context of perioperative chemoimmunotherapy for stage III NSCLC — a novel application within the rapidly expanding NADIM/CheckMate-816/KEYNOTE-671 standard-of-care framework. However, the general premise (ctDNA MRD predicts relapse in NSCLC) is well established (refs 11, 14, 15) and the conceptual advance is incremental — using MRD to refine pCR-based risk stratification. The specific finding that serial two-time-point MRD negativity identifies long-term survivors is clinically meaningful but not first-in-class.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-structured, with a clear rationale, methods, and results flow. The discussion is balanced — acknowledging that the study was not originally designed for MRD and that multiple platforms differ in sensitivity. The case narrative of the single relapse in the MRD-negative group (brain metastasis, 26.9 months OS) is appropriately contextualized. Figures clearly display KM curves for overall, serial-negative, and non-pCR sub-analyses. Minor issues include the mutation notation 'c.480_481delinsCT' which could be verified for accuracy and occasional typos ('7.7 months from MRD to relapse' median clarity).

key_strengths: Exploratory but rigorous biomarker analysis embedded in the randomized NADIM II phase 2 trial with high evaluable rate (60/73 resected, 83/86 samples QC-passed across three batches)
Formal likelihood-ratio testing demonstrating MRD adds prognostic information beyond pCR for both EFS (P<0.001) and OS (P=0.015)
Clinically meaningful finding that serial two-time-point MRD negativity identifies non-pCR patients with survival comparable to pCR patients, enabling future de-escalation trial design
Tumor-agnostic epigenomic assay avoids tissue dependency, has LOQ 0.01%, and validated orthogonally by matching a TP53 variant between tumor and post-op ctDNA in one case
key_concerns: Sub-study was not originally powered for MRD; low MRD-positive rate (9.6%) results in wide CIs (e.g., HR for the single relapse 41.6, 95% CI 5.0-348.8)
Tumor-agnostic assay has lower sensitivity than tumor-informed platforms (e.g., PhasED-Seq, MAESTRO), potentially underestimating MRD in some patients
Only 25 of 60 patients had two consecutive samples for the most impactful sub-analysis, limiting generalizability of the serial-negative strategy
No prospective validation of MRD-guided de-escalation is performed; findings are hypothesis-generating
Single-platform and single-trial context limits cross-assay generalizability
chief_reviewer.rationale: A thoughtful prospective biomarker sub-study of a randomized trial with formally demonstrated incremental prognostic value over pCR; tier 2 (e.g., Clinical Cancer Research, Cancer Research, ESMO Open, JCO Precision Oncology) is plausible at its highest, with tier 1 precluded by small sample size, exploratory/post-hoc nature, and single-platform assay.
